title.en: Internal structure of root, stem and leaf: dicot and monocot

text.en: If you slice a thin section of a sunflower stem and a maize stem and look at both under a microscope, the bundles are arranged in two completely different ways. That one clue tells you which is a dicot and which a monocot.

The dicot root (bean) has an epiblema with unicellular root hairs, a cortex, an endodermis with Casparian strips and passage cells, a pericycle where lateral roots begin, a tetrarch radial bundle and usually no pith.
The monocot root (maize) is polyarch with a large pith; its conjunctive tissue is sclerenchyma and it does not undergo secondary growth.
The dicot stem (sunflower) has an epidermis, a cortex of collenchyma, chlorenchyma and parenchyma, an endodermis called the starch sheath, and conjoint collateral open endarch bundles in a ring around a pith.
The monocot stem (maize) has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, undifferentiated ground tissue and many scattered, skull-shaped conjoint collateral closed bundles, each with a bundle sheath.
The dicot leaf (mango) is dorsiventral: upper epidermis, mesophyll divided into palisade and spongy parenchyma, and lower epidermis with more stomata.
The monocot leaf (grass) is isobilateral: mesophyll is not divided into palisade and spongy tissue, stomata are on both surfaces and bulliform cells are present in the upper epidermis.
Remember the contrast: dicot root is tetrarch, monocot root polyarch; dicot stem bundles are in a ring and open, monocot stem bundles are scattered and closed.

problem.en: Identify the stem: it has a ring of 8 vascular bundles, cambium between xylem and phloem, and a large pith.

text.en: Bundles arranged in a ring suggests a dicot.

why.en: Open bundles are conjoint, collateral and open.

text.en: So it is a dicot stem such as sunflower.

prompt.en: List four differences between a dicot stem and a monocot stem.

points.en: Dicot root: tetrarch; monocot root: polyarch with large pith.
Dicot stem: ring of open bundles, differentiated ground tissue.
Monocot stem: scattered closed bundles with bundle sheath.
Dicot leaf has palisade and spongy tissue; monocot leaf has bulliform cells and stomata on both sides.
